items.exampleCN: 它把 ministrare 变成 administrare。

items.example: The noun is the servant at the centre of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整族词中央那个「仆人」。

items.example: It is the verb behind administer.
items.exampleCN: 它是 administer 背后的动词。

items.example: The compound verb adds direction to service.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词在「服务」之上加了方向。

items.example: It forms administration from administrare.
items.exampleCN: 它把 administrare 构成 administration。

items.example: It forms administrative.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 administrative。

items.example: It forms administrator.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 administrator。

items.example: The word keeps the service sense in a modern office.
items.exampleCN: 这个词在现代部门名称里保留了「服务」义。

definition_zh: 值得钦佩的；令人赞赏的；出色的；令人敬佩的勇气；可贵的品质；可赞美的事；克制的表现；极好的
definition_en: deserving respect and approval because of good qualities, actions, or achievements
core_image: 众人抬头看向台上那个人，目光停住，心里升起一句「值得敬佩」
scene: 博物馆的展厅里，人群在旧照片前安静下来，一位老人站得笔直。Her calm dignity in the crowded hall was truly admirable.
sceneCN: 这里 admirable 是「值得钦佩的」（第 1 个义项：因品格或行为而值得尊敬）；句意为她在拥挤大厅中的从容与尊严确实令人钦佩。

pos.zh: 形容词：值得钦佩的；令人赞赏的；出色的

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉形容词后缀 -able 得到的动词，义为「钦佩；欣赏」
由 admirable 变 -able 为 -ably 构成副词，义为「令人钦佩地；出色地」
由 admirable 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「令人钦佩之处」
由拉丁词基 admir- 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「钦佩；赞赏」
由 admire 加表示施动者的后缀 -er 构成，义为「钦佩者；爱慕者」

senses.title: Deserving respect and approval
senses.definition: deserving to be respected and approved of because of good qualities or actions
senses.definitionCN: 因良好的品格或行为而值得尊敬与赞许
senses.example: Her patience under pressure was admirable.
senses.exampleCN: 她在压力下的耐心令人钦佩。
senses.why: The core image is a head raised toward someone: what is seen there earns respect before any word is spoken.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是抬头望向某人：看到的东西先赢得敬意，话还没有说出口。

senses.title: Arousing praise or pleasure
senses.definition: causing someone to feel praise or pleasure when they see or hear it
senses.definitionCN: 让人看到或听到之后产生赞赏与愉悦
senses.example: The choir gave an admirable performance.
senses.exampleCN: 合唱团献上了一场令人赞赏的演出。
senses.why: The raised eyes now bring pleasure as well as respect: the thing is not only good but good to behold.
senses.whyCN: 抬起的目光如今除了敬意还带来愉悦：对象不只是好，而且看着就让人愉快。

senses.title: Of especially high quality
senses.definition: especially good in quality, skill, or achievement
senses.definitionCN: 在质量、技艺或成就上格外好
senses.example: He wrote an admirable account of the long voyage.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那次远航写得十分出色。
senses.why: Respect hardens into a judgement of quality: the thing admired is placed above the ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 敬意凝固为对质量的判断：被钦佩之物被放到寻常水准之上。

senses.title: Admirable courage: bravery worth respecting
senses.definition: used of courage that deserves respect because it is shown in a hard or dangerous situation
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述在艰难或危险处境中表现出的、值得尊敬的勇气
senses.example: The firefighters showed admirable courage in the blaze.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员在火场中表现出令人敬佩的勇气。
senses.why: Courage is the quality that most clearly earns the raised gaze, because it is shown at a cost.
senses.whyCN: 勇气是最能赢得那道仰望目光的品质，因为它总是以付出为代价显现。

senses.title: Admirable quality: a valuable trait
senses.definition: used of a personal quality that is worth praising and worth keeping
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述值得赞扬、值得保有的个人品质
senses.example: Honesty is an admirable quality in any leader.
senses.exampleCN: 诚实在任何领导者身上都是可贵的品质。
senses.why: The gaze moves from a deed to the trait behind it: what is praised is the lasting disposition.
senses.whyCN: 目光从一次行为移到行为背后的特质：被赞美的是那种持久的品性。

senses.title: Worthy of praise as an act
senses.definition: used of an action that deserves praise rather than blame
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述应当受到赞扬而非责备的行为
senses.example: Her decision to speak out was admirable.
senses.exampleCN: 她决定公开说出真相，这件事值得赞美。
senses.why: Here the judgement falls on a single act: the raised gaze approves what was done, not who did it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的判断落在一个具体行为上：那道仰望的目光认可「做了什么」，而不论是谁做的。

senses.title: Admirable restraint: controlled behaviour
senses.definition: used of self-control that earns respect, especially when anger or reply is held back
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述赢得尊敬的自我克制，尤指忍住怒气或不作回击
senses.example: He met the insult with admirable restraint.
senses.exampleCN: 他以令人钦佩的克制面对那句侮辱。
senses.why: Restraint is courage turned inward: the person holds back, and the held-back force is what earns respect.
senses.whyCN: 克制是向内收住的勇气：人忍住了，而被忍住的那股力量正是赢得敬意之处。

senses.title: Extremely good in informal praise
senses.definition: in informal speech, used to mean extremely good, impressive, or well done
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中表示「极好的、令人印象深刻、干得漂亮」
senses.example: That was an admirable catch at the last second.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一秒的那次接球真是漂亮。
senses.why: The word loosens in talk: respect becomes a warm, casual compliment rather than a solemn judgement.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在口语里松动了：敬意变成一句温和随意的称赞，而不再是一本正经的评判。

intro.en: Admirable is admire plus the suffix -able, and both rest on a Latin verb of wondering.
intro.cn: admirable 是 admire 加后缀 -able 构成的形容词，两者都建立在拉丁语中表示「惊奇」的动词上。

items.en: mirari meant 'to wonder at, be amazed'; it comes from mirus 'wonderful'. The deeper origin of the root is source uncertain.
items.cn: mirari 意为「惊奇、惊叹」，来自 mirus「奇妙的」；该词根更早的来源不确定。

items.en: ad- 'to, at' plus mirari gave admirari, 'to wonder at, regard with admiration'.
items.cn: ad-「向、对」加 mirari 构成 admirari，意为「对……感到惊奇、以钦佩的目光看待」。

items.en: The adjective admirabilis meant 'worthy of wonder, wonderful'; -bilis marks what can or deserves to be done.
items.cn: 形容词 admirabilis 意为「值得惊叹的、奇妙的」；后缀 -bilis 表示「可被……或值得被……」。

items.en: English took the word through French, keeping both the 'wondrous' and the 'praiseworthy' senses.
items.cn: 英语经法语吸收这个词，同时保留了「奇妙的」与「值得赞扬的」两层意思。

items.en: -able became a living English suffix, and the meaning narrowed from wonder to praise of good qualities.
items.cn: -able 成为能产的英语后缀，词义也从「惊奇」收窄为对良好品质的赞扬。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the admiration word family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of praise with different strength.
note.cn: 形近组收 admiration 这一词族；近义组收表示赞扬的形容词，力度各不相同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to respect and look at someone or something with approval.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「钦佩、欣赏」，指带着赞许去敬重或观看某人某物。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a way that deserves praise.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「令人钦佩地、出色地」，指以值得赞扬的方式。

entries.definition: The noun for the feeling of respect and warm approval.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「钦佩、赞赏」，指尊敬与温暖赞许的感受。

entries.definition: A noun for a person who admires someone, often romantically.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「钦佩者、爱慕者」，常指怀有爱慕之情的人。

entries.definition: A naval officer of high rank; it only looks close, since it comes from Arabic amir.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海军上将」；只是拼写相近，词源来自阿拉伯语 amir，与钦佩无关。

entries.definition: Deserving praise, often for effort or intention rather than lasting quality.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「值得称赞的」，多因努力或善意而值得赞扬，而非因持久的品质。

entries.definition: Extremely good in quality; a general judgement with no image of respect.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「极好的」，是一般性的质量判断，不含「敬意」的意象。

entries.definition: Deserving formal praise, especially for an action or effort.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「值得表扬的」，语气正式，多用于行为或努力。

entries.definition: Making a strong effect on the mind, often by size or skill.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人印象深刻的」，多因规模或技艺而震撼人心。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb of wondering and the suffixes that build the family.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「惊奇」动词，以及构成这一词族的后缀。

normal.en: mirari means to wonder, so admirable first meant 'wonderful' before it meant 'praiseworthy'.
normal.cn: mirari 意为「惊奇」，所以 admirable 先有「奇妙的」义，后来才有「值得赞扬的」义。

normal.en: The ad- in admire and admirable points the wonder at a particular person or thing.
normal.cn: admire 与 admirable 中的 ad- 把这份惊奇指向某个具体的人或物。

normal.en: Admiration, admirer and admirably all keep the same admir- base.
normal.cn: admiration、admirer、admirably 都保留同一个 admir- 词基。

normal.en: Admirable courage and admirable restraint name two qualities that cost the person something.
normal.cn: admirable courage 与 admirable restraint 都指需要当事人付出代价的品质。

normal.en: Admiral looks similar but comes from Arabic amir, so it is a false friend.
normal.cn: admiral 看起来相近，却来自阿拉伯语 amir，是个假朋友。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd raising its eyes to a stage: no one speaks, yet respect fills the room.
abstract.cn: 想象人群把目光抬向舞台：没有人说话，敬意却充满整个房间。

abstract.en: The same raised eyes can rest on a brave act, a fine painting, or a quietly held temper.
abstract.cn: 同一双抬起的眼睛，可以停在勇敢的行为、精美的画作，或一份默默忍住的脾气上。

abstract.en: When the gaze softens into a smile, the solemn word becomes everyday praise for a clever catch.
abstract.cn: 当目光软化成微笑，这个庄重的词就变成对一次巧妙接球的日常称赞。

examples.en: Her patience under pressure was truly admirable.
examples.cn: 她在压力下的耐心确实令人钦佩。

examples.en: The team made an admirable effort to finish on time.
examples.cn: 团队为按时完成付出了值得赞赏的努力。

examples.en: He accepted the criticism with admirable calm.
examples.cn: 他以令人钦佩的平静接受了批评。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德默勒布尔」——台下众人抬头看着台上，心里浮出一句「值得敬佩」

root: 拉丁语 admirari「对……感到惊奇、钦佩」由 ad-「向」加 mirari「惊奇」构成，mirari 又来自 mirus「奇妙的」。加形容词后缀 -abilis（英语作 -able）构成 admirabilis，义为「值得惊叹的」。mirari 更早的词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all start from a raised gaze: respect for a person, pleasure at a sight, high quality, courage, a trait, an act, restraint, and casual praise.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一道仰望的目光出发：对人的敬意、观看时的愉悦、高超的质量、勇气、品质、行为、克制，以及随口的称赞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes are raised toward someone, and respect rises with them before any word is spoken.
core.cn: 核心意象：目光抬向某人，敬意随之升起，话还没有出口。

branches.en: THE PERSON: respect for good character and the pleasure of watching it.
branches.cn: 人的线：对良好品格的敬意，以及观看它时的愉悦。

branches.en: THE STANDARD: respect settles into a judgement that something is above the ordinary.
branches.cn: 标准线：敬意沉淀为判断，认定某物高于寻常水准。

branches.en: THE QUALITIES: courage in danger and a trait that is worth keeping.
branches.cn: 品质线：危难中的勇气，以及值得保有的品性。

branches.en: THE ACTS: a single deed worth praise, and a temper quietly held back.
branches.cn: 行为线：一件值得赞美的行为，以及一份默默忍住的脾气。

branches.en: THE COMPLIMENT: in talk the solemn gaze relaxes into warm, casual praise.
branches.cn: 称赞线：在口语里，庄重的目光放松成温和随意的赞扬。

intro.en: Admirable is a Latin adjective reshaped in English; its suffix -able is still productive today.
intro.cn: admirable 是在英语中改造过的拉丁形容词，它的后缀 -able 至今仍能产。

latinIntro.en: mirus, mirari, admirari and admirabilis are all recorded Latin forms; only the original root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: mirus、mirari、admirari、admirabilis 都是有记录的拉丁形式，只有最初的词根属于重构。

items.example: It turns mirari into admirari.
items.exampleCN: 它把 mirari 变成 admirari。

items.example: The adjective is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是整族词的词根。

items.example: The verb supplies the idea of wonder.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了「惊奇」的观念。

items.example: The compound verb is the direct source of admire.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词是 admire 的直接来源。

items.example: It is the Latin shape behind admirable.
items.exampleCN: 它是 admirable 背后的拉丁语形态。

items.meaning: able to be, worthy of being
items.example: It forms admirable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admirable。

items.example: It forms admirably.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admirably。

items.example: It forms admiration.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admiration。

items.example: It forms admirer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admirer。

definition_zh: 钦佩；欣赏；仰慕；赞美；观赏；因……而钦佩；暗自赞叹；惊奇（旧义）
definition_en: to respect and approve of someone or something, often while looking at them with pleasure or wonder
core_image: 抬头望着高处的一幅画，目光停住，敬意从心里升起
scene: 毕业典礼上，礼堂里坐满家长，灯光照着台上那位最后发言的学生。The whole hall admired the courage of the girl who spoke last.
sceneCN: 这里 admire 是「钦佩」（第 1 个义项：因某人的品质或行为而敬重）；句意为全场都钦佩那位最后发言的女孩的勇气。

pos.zh: 动词：钦佩；欣赏；仰慕；赞美；观赏

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词基 admir- 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「钦佩；赞赏」
由 admire 加表示施动者的后缀 -er 构成，义为「钦佩者；爱慕者」
由 admire 加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「值得钦佩的；出色的」
由 admire 加现在分词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「表示钦佩的；赞赏的」
由 admiring 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「钦佩地；赞赏地」

senses.title: To respect a person for their qualities
senses.definition: to respect and approve of a person because of their abilities, character, or achievements
senses.definitionCN: 因某人的能力、品格或成就而敬重、赞许其人
senses.example: I admire her for the way she handled the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 我钦佩她处理这场危机的方式。
senses.why: The core image is eyes raised toward a person: respect is the first thing that rises with the gaze.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是目光抬向某人：敬意是随目光一同升起的第一样东西。

senses.title: To appreciate an object with pleasure
senses.definition: to look at or think about an object with pleasure and approval
senses.definitionCN: 带着愉悦与赞许去观看或思量某件物品
senses.example: We stopped on the bridge to admire the old stonework.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在桥上停下来欣赏那些古老的石雕。
senses.why: The gaze moves from a person to a thing, and approval becomes the pleasure of looking.
senses.whyCN: 目光从人移向物，赞许就变成了观看时的愉悦。

senses.title: To feel silent devotion toward someone
senses.definition: to regard someone with deep, often silent devotion from a distance
senses.definitionCN: 从远处怀着深切而往往沉默的爱慕看待某人
senses.example: As a student he admired his teacher from a distance.
senses.exampleCN: 学生时代，他远远地仰慕着自己的老师。
senses.why: When the raised gaze never lowers, respect grows warm and quiet, and becomes devotion.
senses.whyCN: 当那道仰望的目光始终没有落下，敬意就变得温热而安静，成为爱慕。

senses.title: To praise someone openly
senses.definition: to speak or write about someone's good qualities with open approval
senses.definitionCN: 公开地谈论或书写某人的优点，表示赞许
senses.example: The critic admired the young painter's use of colour.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家赞美了这位年轻画家对色彩的运用。
senses.why: The inner respect now leaves the eyes and enters words: what was seen is said aloud.
senses.whyCN: 内心的敬意离开眼睛、进入言语：看见的东西被说了出来。

senses.title: To look at a view with enjoyment
senses.definition: to look at a view or scene with enjoyment and appreciation
senses.definitionCN: 带着愉悦与赏识观看一片景色或场景
senses.example: They sat on the terrace and admired the sunset over the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 他们坐在露台上观赏海湾上的日落。
senses.why: Here the object is wide and distant: the raised gaze sweeps a whole view instead of one person.
senses.whyCN: 这里的对象开阔而遥远：仰望的目光扫过整片景色，而不是一个人。

senses.title: To respect someone because of a particular act
senses.definition: in the pattern admire someone for something, to respect them because of a specific act or quality
senses.definitionCN: 用于 admire someone for something 结构，因某个具体行为或品质而敬重其人
senses.example: We admire him for refusing to take the easy way out.
senses.exampleCN: 我们钦佩他拒绝走捷径。
senses.why: The preposition for names the exact thing that drew the gaze: respect is pinned to one deed.
senses.whyCN: 介词 for 点明吸引目光的具体之处：敬意被钉在某一件事上。

senses.title: To marvel at something in silence
senses.definition: to feel quiet wonder at something without saying it aloud
senses.definitionCN: 对某物怀有安静的惊叹，却不宣之于口
senses.example: She admired the skill in his hands and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 她暗自赞叹他手上的功夫，却什么也没说。
senses.why: Wonder stays inside the gazer: the eyes widen, the mouth stays shut, and the praise is never spoken.
senses.whyCN: 惊奇留在观看者心里：眼睛睁大，嘴却闭着，赞美始终没有说出口。

senses.title: To wonder at, in older usage
senses.definition: in older English, to wonder at something with surprise, now found mainly in literary or historical texts
senses.definitionCN: 在早期英语中表示「对……感到惊奇」，今多见于文学作品或历史文本
senses.example: The old poem bids the reader admire at the strangeness of the world.
senses.exampleCN: 那首古诗请读者对世界的奇异感到惊奇。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: before respect, admire simply meant to be struck by wonder.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：在「敬意」之前，admire 只表示被惊奇击中。

intro.en: Admire comes from Latin admirari, and its first meaning in English was closer to 'wonder at' than to 'respect'.
intro.cn: admire 来自拉丁语 admirari，它在英语里最早的意思更接近「感到惊奇」，而不是「敬重」。

items.en: mirus meant 'wonderful, strange'; its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: mirus 意为「奇妙的、奇异的」；它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The verb mirari meant 'to wonder at, be amazed', a deponent verb with a passive form and active sense.
items.cn: 动词 mirari 意为「惊奇、惊叹」，是一个形式被动而意义主动的异态动词。

items.en: ad- 'to, at' plus mirari gave admirari, 'to wonder at, regard with admiration'.
items.cn: ad-「向、对」加 mirari 构成 admirari，意为「对……感到惊奇、以钦佩之心看待」。

items.en: English borrowed the word through French; early uses still carried the strong sense of wonder and surprise.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入这个词；早期用法仍带着强烈的「惊奇、诧异」意味。

items.en: The sense shifted toward esteem and approval, while the old 'wonder at' survives mainly in literary phrasing.
items.cn: 词义逐渐转向敬重与赞许，而旧的「感到惊奇」义主要残存在文学表达中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same admir- root; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of esteem and devotion.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 admir- 词根的一族词；近义组收其他表示敬重与爱慕的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the feeling of respect and warm approval.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「钦佩、赞赏」，指尊敬与温暖赞许的感受。

entries.definition: A person who admires someone, often with romantic feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「钦佩者、爱慕者」，常指怀有爱慕之情的人。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning deserving respect and approval.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「值得钦佩的、令人赞赏的」。

entries.definition: An adjective describing a look or remark that shows admiration.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「表示钦佩的、赞赏的」，用于描述目光或言语。

entries.definition: A high-ranking naval officer; the similarity is only in spelling, since it comes from Arabic amir.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海军上将」；只是拼写相近，词源来自阿拉伯语 amir。

entries.definition: To regard someone as worthy of esteem; cooler and less visual than admire.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「尊敬」，比 admire 更冷静，也没有「仰望观看」的意象。

entries.definition: To hold someone in high regard; formal and often about judgement rather than feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「敬重」，语气正式，多指评价而非情感。

entries.definition: To honour with religious devotion or excessive respect.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「崇拜、敬奉」，带宗教虔诚或过度的敬意。

entries.definition: To recognize the value of something with pleasure; less personal than admire.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欣赏、赏识」，指领会某物的价值并感到愉快，比 admire 少些个人情感。

entries.definition: To feel deep respect and awe; stronger and more solemn than admire.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「崇敬」，带深切的敬畏，语气比 admire 更庄重强烈。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb of wondering and the patterns admire actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「惊奇」动词，以及 admire 实际出现的搭配结构。

normal.en: The oldest sense is wonder: mirari, the Latin source, means to be amazed.
normal.cn: 最古老的意思是惊奇：它的拉丁来源 mirari 就是「感到惊讶」。

normal.en: admire somebody for something pins the respect to one specific act.
normal.cn: admire somebody for something 把敬意固定在某一件具体的行为上。

normal.en: Admiration, admirer and admirable all keep the admir- base and change only the suffix.
normal.cn: admiration、admirer、admirable 都保留 admir- 词基，只更换后缀。

normal.en: You admire a view with your eyes and admire a person with your judgement.
normal.cn: 看景色时用眼睛 admire，看人时用判断 admire。

normal.en: Admiral is a false friend from Arabic amir, not a relative of admire.
normal.cn: admiral 是来自阿拉伯语 amir 的假朋友，与 admire 并无亲缘。

abstract.en: Picture a face lifted toward a high window, eyes fixed, mouth closed: that is respect before it becomes a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸抬向高窗，目光定住，嘴闭着：那就是还没变成语言的敬意。

abstract.en: The same lifted face can rest on a stone bridge, a sunset, or a quiet pair of hands.
abstract.cn: 同一张仰起的脸，可以停在石桥、日落，或一双安静的手上。

abstract.en: When the mouth finally opens, the silent gaze turns into praise; when it stays shut, the wonder remains private.
abstract.cn: 嘴终于张开时，沉默的目光变成赞美；嘴一直闭着时，惊奇就留在心里。

examples.en: She admired the patience with which he taught the children.
examples.cn: 她钦佩他教孩子时的那份耐心。

examples.en: We stood on the cliff and admired the wide blue bay.
examples.cn: 我们站在悬崖上，观赏宽阔的蓝色海湾。

examples.en: Many readers still admire the clarity of her early essays.
examples.cn: 许多读者至今仍赞赏她早期随笔的清晰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额的迈尔」——抬头仰望，目光停住，敬意从心里慢慢升起

root: 拉丁语 admirari「对……感到惊奇、钦佩」由 ad-「向」加 mirari「惊奇」构成，mirari 又来自 mirus「奇妙的」。英语经古法语借入后，词义由「惊奇」逐渐转向「敬重、赞赏」；表示「感到惊奇」的旧义仍残存在文学用法中。更早词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin with a raised gaze: respect for a person, pleasure in an object, silent devotion, open praise, a wide view, a specific deed, private wonder, and the old sense of amazement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都始于一道仰望的目光：对人的敬重、对物的愉悦、沉默的爱慕、公开的赞美、开阔的景色、具体的行为、私下的惊叹，以及古老的「惊奇」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gaze is lifted and held, and respect rises quietly behind the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：目光抬起并停住，敬意在眼睛背后悄悄升起。

branches.en: THE PERSON: respect for someone, and the same feeling kept silent inside the gazer.
branches.cn: 人的线：对某人的敬重，以及留在观看者心里的同一种沉默情感。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: an object or a whole view enjoyed through the eyes.
branches.cn: 物件线：一件物品或整片景色，通过眼睛被愉悦地领受。

branches.en: THE HEART: when the gaze never lowers, respect warms into devotion.
branches.cn: 情感线：当目光始终不落下，敬意就升温为爱慕。

branches.en: THE VOICE: the inner respect leaves the eyes and becomes spoken praise.
branches.cn: 言语线：内心的敬意离开眼睛，变成说出口的赞美。

branches.en: THE ANCHOR AND THE ORIGIN: one deed fixes the respect, while wonder is the oldest layer.
branches.cn: 锚点与源头线：一件行为把敬意固定下来，而「惊奇」是最古老的一层。

intro.en: Admire is a Latin verb with an English life; its family is built with ordinary noun, adjective and adverb suffixes.
intro.cn: admire 是一个在英语中生活的拉丁动词，它的词族由普通的名词、形容词与副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: mirus, mirari and admirari are all recorded Latin forms, so only the base root needs reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: mirus、mirari、admirari 都是有记录的拉丁形式，只有基础词根需要重构。

items.example: It directs the wonder toward an object.
items.exampleCN: 它把惊奇指向某个对象。

items.example: It is the adjective at the root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族根部的形容词。

items.example: The verb carries the original sense of amazement.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词承载着最初的「惊奇」义。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: It forms admiration.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admiration。

items.example: It forms admirer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admirer。

items.example: It forms admirable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admirable。

items.example: It forms admiring.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admiring。

items.example: It forms admiringly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admiringly。

definition_zh: 承认；入场许可；入场费；入学录取；接纳加入；坦白供认；入院；认罪
definition_en: the act of allowing someone to enter, or a statement in which someone accepts that something is true
core_image: 门卫看过证件，抬起手放行：门开的一刻，既是被准许进入，也是被承认为自己人
scene: 医院大厅的取号机旁，一位老人扶着墙慢慢坐下，家属忙着填写表格。Her admission to the hospital was arranged for the next morning.
sceneCN: 这里 admission 是「入院」（第 7 个义项：作为病人被医院接收）；句意为她入院的手续被安排在第二天早上。

pos.zh: 名词：承认；入场许可；入场费；入学录取；入院

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀 -sion 得到的动词，义为「承认；准许进入；接纳」
由 admit 加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「进入权」，多用于正式告示
由 admit 加形容词后缀 -ible 构成，义为「可采纳的；可接受的」
由 admissible 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可采纳性」
由 admitted 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「诚然；无可否认地」

senses.title: A statement that something is true
senses.definition: a statement in which someone agrees that something is true, often unwillingly
senses.definitionCN: 某人同意某件事属实的陈述，往往并不情愿
senses.example: His admission that he had lied surprised the whole room.
senses.exampleCN: 他承认自己说了谎，这让满屋子的人都感到意外。
senses.why: The core image is a gate opening: to admit a fact is to let it inside instead of keeping it outside.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是门被打开：承认一个事实，就是把它放进来，而不是挡在门外。

senses.title: Permission to enter a place
senses.definition: the right or permission given to someone to enter a place
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人进入某处的权利或许可
senses.example: Admission is allowed only with a staff card.
senses.exampleCN: 只有持员工卡才准许进入。
senses.why: This is the gate at its most literal: the hand is raised, and the person is let through.
senses.whyCN: 这是「门」最字面的意义：手抬起来，人就通过了。

senses.title: The price paid to enter
senses.definition: the amount of money charged for entering a place such as a museum or theatre
senses.definitionCN: 进入博物馆、剧院等场所所需缴纳的费用
senses.example: The admission to the gallery is ten dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 进入这家画廊的入场费是十美元。
senses.why: Permission has a price: the gate opens only when the ticket, not just the hand, is raised.
senses.whyCN: 许可是有价的：光抬手还不够，票也要递上去，门才开。

senses.title: Acceptance into a school or course
senses.definition: the act of being accepted as a student at a school, college, or university
senses.definitionCN: 被学校、学院或大学接收为学生
senses.example: She received admission to three universities.
senses.exampleCN: 她被三所大学录取。
senses.why: The gate is now a school gate: being let in means being judged ready to enter.
senses.whyCN: 这里的门成了校门：被放行意味着被认定有资格进来。

senses.title: Acceptance into a group or organization
senses.definition: the act of accepting someone as a member of a group or organization
senses.definitionCN: 接收某人为某个团体或组织的成员
senses.example: The club voted on the admission of new members.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部就接纳新成员一事进行了表决。
senses.why: The gate surrounds a circle of people: to be admitted is to be counted inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这道门围着一圈人：被接纳，就是被算进圈内。

senses.title: A confession of wrongdoing
senses.definition: a statement in which someone accepts that they have done something wrong
senses.definitionCN: 某人承认自己做了错事的陈述
senses.example: His admission came only after hours of questioning.
senses.exampleCN: 经过数小时讯问，他才坦白供认。
senses.why: The gate opens inward on something ugly: the wrongdoer lets the truth in against himself.
senses.whyCN: 这道门向内打开，放进来的是难看的东西：做错事的人违背自身利益把真相放进来。

senses.title: Being received into hospital
senses.definition: the act of being received into hospital as a patient for treatment
senses.definitionCN: 作为病人被医院接收以接受治疗
senses.example: Her admission to the hospital was arranged for the next morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她入院的手续被安排在第二天早上。
senses.why: A hospital gate lets a sick body through: the person is taken in so that care can begin.
senses.whyCN: 医院的门放一副病体通过：人被收进来，照料才得以开始。

senses.title: Admission of guilt in legal use
senses.definition: in law, the formal phrase admission of guilt, a statement accepting responsibility for an offence
senses.definitionCN: 法律用语，指正式承认对某项罪行负有责任的陈述
senses.example: The signed statement served as an admission of guilt.
senses.exampleCN: 这份签字声明起到了认罪的作用。
senses.why: Law fixes the open gate into a document: the confession becomes evidence with a name.
senses.whyCN: 法律把敞开的门固定成一份文件：供认变成有名称的证据。

intro.en: Admission is the noun of the verb admit, and both go back to a Latin verb meaning 'to send in'.
intro.cn: admission 是动词 admit 的名词形式，两者都可上溯到意为「送进去」的拉丁动词。

items.en: mittere meant 'to send, let go'; it is the source of mission, message and many compounds.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送出、放行」，是 mission、message 以及许多复合词的来源。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus mittere gave admittere, 'to let in, allow to enter, grant'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 mittere 构成 admittere，意为「放进去、准许进入、允许」。

items.en: The noun admissio named the act of letting in, and also the audience granted to a visitor.
items.cn: 名词 admissio 表示「放行、准许进入」，也指接见来客。

items.en: English took admission through French; the sense of a confession appears later than the sense of entry.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入 admission；「承认、供认」义比「进入」义出现得更晚。

items.en: The word split into concrete gates, school places, hospital beds, and the abstract act of accepting a truth.
items.cn: 这个词分化为具体的门、学校的名额、医院的床位，以及接受某一真相的抽象行为。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same admit family; the near-meaning group gathers words for entering, accepting, and confessing.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 admit 词族的形式；近义组收表示进入、接纳与供认的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to confess, to let in, or to have room for.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认、准许进入、容纳」，是本词的动词形式。

entries.definition: A noun meaning the right to enter a place, used especially on official signs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入权」，尤见于正式告示，如「禁止入内」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning allowed to be used or accepted, especially as evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可采纳的、可接受的」，尤指证据。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being acceptable, especially in court.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可采纳性」，尤用于法庭。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning it must be admitted that; used to concede a point.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「诚然、无可否认」，用于让步承认某一点。

entries.definition: The act of coming in, or a doorway; plainer than admission and without the idea of permission.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入、入口」，比 admission 朴素，不含「获准」的意思。

entries.definition: A way in or the act of entering; often physical rather than official.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「入口、进入」，多指物理上的通道而非官方许可。

entries.definition: A formal statement admitting guilt, often religious or legal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「供认、忏悔」，语气常带宗教或法律色彩。

entries.definition: The act of agreeing to take something or someone; broader than admission.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接受、接纳」，范围比 admission 更宽。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「注册、入学」，与 admission 的入学义接近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb 'to send in' and the family built on admit.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁动词「送进去」，以及建立在 admit 上的词族。

normal.en: mittere means to send, so admit is literally to send someone in.
normal.cn: mittere 意为「送」，所以 admit 字面上就是「把人送进去」。

normal.en: Admission and admittance both name a letting in, but admittance survives mainly on official signs.
normal.cn: admission 与 admittance 都表示「放行」，但 admittance 主要残存在正式告示里。

normal.en: Admissible evidence is evidence a court is willing to let in.
normal.cn: admissible evidence 就是法庭愿意「放进来」的证据。

normal.en: Admission of guilt turns an open gate into a signed document.
normal.cn: admission of guilt 把敞开的门变成一份签字的文件。

normal.en: A hospital admission is a bed being opened to a sick body.
normal.cn: hospital admission 就是为病体打开一张床位。

abstract.en: Picture a gatekeeper with one hand raised: the gate is the same whether a visitor, a fact, or a patient comes through.
abstract.cn: 想象门卫抬起一只手：无论进来的是访客、事实还是病人，这道门都一样。

abstract.en: A truth kept outside is a burden; once admitted, it is inside and must be dealt with.
abstract.cn: 被挡在门外的真相是一种负担；一旦被承认，它就进了门，必须被处理。

abstract.en: The same gate becomes a school door, a club door, a ward door, and a courtroom door.
abstract.cn: 同一道门可以变成校门、会所的门、病房的门，以及法庭的门。

examples.en: The admission fee includes a guided tour of the old hall.
examples.cn: 入场费包含一次老厅的导览。

examples.en: His admission that he was wrong ended the argument.
examples.cn: 他承认自己错了，争论就此结束。

examples.en: The hospital sent a letter about her admission next week.
examples.cn: 医院寄来一封信，说明她下周入院。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额的米申」——门卫点头放行，进门那一刻既是许可，也是认账

root: 拉丁语 admittere「放进去、准许进入」由 ad-「向」加 mittere「送、放」构成；其名词 admissio 表示「放行、接见」。mittere 是 mission、message 等词的共同来源。英语经法语借入 admission，先有「进入」义，后发展出「承认、供认」义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all turn on one gate: a fact let in, a person let in, a ticket, a school place, a membership, a confession, a hospital bed, and a legal plea.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都围绕同一道门：放进来一个事实、一个人、一张票、一个学位名额、一个成员资格、一份供认、一张病床，以及一份法律上的认罪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gatekeeper raises a hand and lets something through, whether a person or a truth.
core.cn: 核心意象：门卫抬起手放行，通过的东西可以是人，也可以是一个真相。

branches.en: THE TRUTH: a fact or a fault is let in, and the gate opens inward against the speaker.
branches.cn: 真话线：一个事实或一桩过失被放进来，门朝着说话人不利的方向向内开。

branches.en: THE DOCUMENT: law turns the spoken confession into a signed admission of guilt.
branches.cn: 文件线：法律把口头供认变成签字的认罪声明。

branches.en: THE GATE: permission to enter, and the ticket that buys that permission.
branches.cn: 门线：进入的许可，以及买来这份许可的票。

branches.en: THE CIRCLE: a school place or a membership is being counted inside a group.
branches.cn: 圈子线：一个学位名额或成员资格，就是被算进某个群体之内。

branches.en: THE WARD: a hospital opens its gate to a sick body so that care can begin.
branches.cn: 病房线：医院为病体打开大门，照料从此开始。

intro.en: Admission is built from a Latin prefix, the send root, and a noun suffix; English adds further endings for the family.
intro.cn: admission 由拉丁语前缀、表示「送」的词根与名词后缀构成；英语再为词族添加其他词尾。

latinIntro.en: mittere, admittere, admissio and missio are all recorded Latin words; only the older root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: mittere、admittere、admissio、missio 都是有记录的拉丁词，只有更早的词根属于重构。

items.example: It turns mittere into admittere.
items.exampleCN: 它把 mittere 变成 admittere。

items.example: The verb is the send root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「送」词根。

items.example: It is the direct source of admit.
items.exampleCN: 它是 admit 的直接来源。

items.example: It is the Latin shape behind admission.
items.exampleCN: 它是 admission 背后的拉丁语形态。

items.example: It forms admission from admissio.
items.exampleCN: 它把 admissio 构成 admission。

items.example: It forms admittance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admittance。

items.example: It forms admissible.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admissible。

items.example: It forms admissibility.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admissibility。

items.example: It forms admittedly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 admittedly。

definition_zh: 承认（事实）；承认（错误或罪行）；准许进入；准许入学；接纳为成员；容纳；容许；收治入院
definition_en: to agree that something is true, or to allow a person or thing to enter
core_image: 沉重的门被推开一条缝：门外的人被放进来，门外的事实也被放进来
scene: 深夜的医院走廊灯光昏黄，值班护士翻着登记簿，推车轮子轻轻响。The nurse admitted the patient to the ward just after midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 admit 是「收治入院」（第 8 个义项：把病人收进医院治疗）；句意为护士在午夜刚过时把病人收进了病房。

pos.zh: 动词：承认；准许进入；接纳；容纳；容许

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -sion 构成，义为「承认；入场许可；入学录取」
由本词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「进入权」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ible 构成，义为「可采纳的；可接受的」
由 admitted 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「诚然；无可否认地」
由 admissible 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可采纳性」

senses.title: To agree that a fact is true
senses.definition: to agree, often unwillingly, that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 往往并不情愿地同意某件事属实
senses.example: He admitted that the plan had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 他承认这个计划失败了。
senses.why: The core image is a door held shut: admitting a fact means overriding the hand that keeps it out.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一扇被抵住的门：承认事实，就是压过那只把真相挡在外面的手。

senses.title: To confess a fault or crime
senses.definition: to state that one has done something wrong or illegal
senses.definitionCN: 陈述自己做过错事或违法之事
senses.example: She admitted stealing the money.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认偷了那笔钱。
senses.why: Here the door opens against oneself: what is let in can be used as evidence.
senses.whyCN: 这里的门是逆着自己打开的：放进来东西可能被当作不利于自己的证据。

senses.title: To allow someone to enter a place
senses.definition: to allow a person or thing to enter a building, room, or area
senses.definitionCN: 允许某人或某物进入建筑、房间或区域
senses.example: The guard admitted us through the side door.
senses.exampleCN: 门卫让我们从侧门进去。
senses.why: This is the physical gate: the body is let through, and the door closes behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理意义上的门：身体被放进去，门在身后合上。

senses.title: To accept a student into a school
senses.definition: to accept someone as a student at a school, college, or university
senses.definitionCN: 接收某人为学校、学院或大学的学生
senses.example: The college admitted two hundred new students this year.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学院今年录取了两百名新生。
senses.why: A school gate opens only to those judged ready, so the letting in is also a verdict.
senses.whyCN: 校门只对被认为合格的人打开，所以「放进来」同时也是一次裁定。

senses.title: To accept someone as a member
senses.definition: to accept a person into a group, club, or organization as a member
senses.definitionCN: 接收某人成为团体、俱乐部或组织的成员
senses.example: The society admitted her as its first woman fellow.
senses.exampleCN: 该学会接纳她为首位女性会士。
senses.why: The gate now encloses a circle: being admitted is being counted among those inside.
senses.whyCN: 此时的门围成一圈：被接纳，就是被算进圈内的人当中。

senses.title: To have room for a number
senses.definition: of a place, to have enough space for a certain number of people or things
senses.definitionCN: 指某场所拥有足够空间容纳一定数量的人或物
senses.example: The hall admits only four hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅只能容纳四百人。
senses.why: A place is a door with a width: what cannot be let in simply has no room inside.
senses.whyCN: 场所像一扇有宽度的门：进不来的东西，只是因为里面没有位置。

senses.title: Admit of: to allow as possible
senses.definition: in the phrase admit of, to allow something as a possible course, reading, or interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 admit of，表示容许某种做法、读法或解释
senses.example: The evidence admits of only one explanation.
senses.exampleCN: 这些证据只容许一种解释。
senses.why: The gate is opened by possibility itself: what a thing admits of is what it can let through.
senses.whyCN: 这道门由「可能性」来开：某物所容许的，就是它能放过去的东西。

senses.title: To receive a patient into hospital
senses.definition: to receive a sick person into a hospital ward for treatment
senses.definitionCN: 把病人收进医院病房接受治疗
senses.example: The nurse admitted the patient to the ward just after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在午夜刚过时把病人收进了病房。
senses.why: The ward gate is opened for a body that needs care: admission here begins a course of treatment.
senses.whyCN: 病房的门为一个需要照料的病体打开：这里的「放进来」意味着一疗程的开始。

intro.en: Admit comes from Latin admittere, literally 'to send in'; the sense of confessing came later than the sense of entering.
intro.cn: admit 来自拉丁语 admittere，字面意思是「送进去」；「承认」义比「进入」义出现得更晚。

items.en: mittere meant 'to send, let go, release'; many English words such as mission and transmit descend from it.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送出、放行、释放」；mission、transmit 等许多英语词都源于它。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus mittere gave admittere, 'to let in, allow access, receive'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 mittere 构成 admittere，意为「放进去、准许进入、接收」。

items.en: Its noun admissio named a letting in and an audience granted to a visitor.
items.cn: 它的名词 admissio 表示「放行」，也指接见来客。

items.en: The verb entered English through French with the sense of allowing entry; the confessing sense is recorded later.
items.cn: 这个动词经法语进入英语，先表示「准许进入」；「承认、供认」义有记录更晚。

items.en: The word now covers everything from letting a person through a door to conceding a fact one would rather deny.
items.cn: 如今这个词覆盖从「放人过门」到「承认一个本不愿承认的事实」的全部用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the admission family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of confessing, allowing, and holding.
note.cn: 形近组收 admission 这一词族；近义组收表示供认、允许与容纳的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for entering, being accepted, or confessing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入、被接纳、承认」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: A noun for the right to enter, common on official notices.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入权」，常见于正式告示。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning allowed to be accepted, especially as evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可采纳的、可接受的」，尤指证据。

entries.definition: An adverb used to concede that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「诚然、无可否认」，用于让步承认某事属实。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being acceptable, especially in court.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可采纳性」，尤用于法庭。

entries.definition: To admit wrongdoing openly; stronger and more formal than admit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「供认、坦白」，比 admit 更强烈、更正式。

entries.definition: To accept that something is true or exists; more neutral than admit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认、确认」，比 admit 更中性。

entries.definition: To permit something to happen or someone to enter; general and neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「允许」，可指允许某事发生或某人进入，一般而中性。

entries.definition: To provide space for a number of people; close to the holding sense of admit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「容纳、提供空间」，与 admit 的「容纳」义接近。

entries.definition: To give official permission; more formal and often written.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「准许」，较正式，多见于书面语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb 'to send in' and the patterns admit actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁动词「送进去」，以及 admit 实际出现的搭配结构。

normal.en: mittere means to send, so admit is to send something or someone inside.
normal.cn: mittere 意为「送」，所以 admit 就是把某物或某人送进门内。

normal.en: Admit that introduces a fact, while admit to often introduces a fault.
normal.cn: admit that 后面多接一个事实，admit to 后面多接一桩过失。

normal.en: Be admitted to a college is to be let through its gate as a student.
normal.cn: be admitted to a college 就是作为学生被放行通过校门。

normal.en: Admit of is the old construction meaning to allow as possible.
normal.cn: admit of 是表示「容许、有……可能」的较旧结构。

normal.en: A hall that admits four hundred people has room for exactly that many.
normal.cn: 「a hall that admits four hundred people」指这个厅刚好能装下那么多人。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy door pushed open only a hand's width: someone outside is let in, or a fact is let in.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇沉重的门只被推开一掌宽：放进来的是门外的人，或门外的事实。

abstract.en: When the door opens inward against the speaker, the word turns from hospitality into confession.
abstract.cn: 当门逆着说话人向内开，这个词就从「款待」变成了「供认」。

abstract.en: The same doorway becomes a school gate, a club door, a ward entrance, and the narrow gap of possibility.
abstract.cn: 同一处门洞可以变成校门、会所的门、病房入口，以及可能性的那道窄缝。

examples.en: He admitted that he had forgotten the appointment.
examples.cn: 他承认自己忘了那次约见。

examples.en: Only ticket holders are admitted to the exhibition.
examples.cn: 只有持票者才被准许进入展览。

examples.en: The small ward admits just six patients at a time.
examples.cn: 这间小病房一次只能容纳六名病人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额的米特」——门开一条缝，先放人进来，再点头认账

root: 拉丁语 admittere「放进去、准许进入」由 ad-「向」加 mittere「送、放行」构成，mittere 也是 mission、transmit 等词的来源。英语经法语借入后，先有「准许进入」义，后发展出「承认、供认」义，并引申出「容纳」与「容许」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all work one doorway: a fact, a fault, a visitor, a student, a member, a crowd, a possibility, and a patient are each let through.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在开同一道门：事实、过失、访客、学生、成员、人群、可能性、病人，各自被放行通过。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy door is pushed open a hand's width, and something outside is let through.
core.cn: 核心意象：沉重的门被推开一掌宽，门外的东西被放行进来。

branches.en: THE TRUTH: a fact or a fault is let in, and the door opens against the speaker.
branches.cn: 真话线：一个事实或一桩过失被放进来，门朝着说话人不利的方向开。

branches.en: THE GATE: a body, a student, or a member is allowed through and counted inside.
branches.cn: 门线：身体、学生或成员被准许通过，并被算进里面。

branches.en: THE ROOM: a place is a door of fixed width, and only so many can pass.
branches.cn: 空间线：场所是一扇宽度固定的门，能通过的只有那么多。

branches.en: THE POSSIBILITY: what a thing admits of is what it can let through.
branches.cn: 可能性线：某物所容许的，就是它能够放过去的东西。

branches.en: THE WARD: a hospital door opens for a sick body, and treatment begins.
branches.cn: 病房线：医院的门为病体打开，治疗由此开始。

definition_zh: 青春期；青春期阶段；少年时期；发育过渡期；青春期的身心变化；青春期人群；青春期的社会阶段；生理成熟期
definition_en: the period of life between childhood and adulthood, when a young person develops physically and emotionally
core_image: 一棵正在抽条的树苗：枝干突然拔高，树皮还没变硬，风一吹就晃
scene: 夏夜的院子里，蝉声不停，几个十几岁的孩子在灯下写作业。During adolescence, sleep patterns often shift later in the evening.
sceneCN: 这里 adolescence 是「青春期」（第 1 个义项：童年与成年之间的成长阶段）；句意为在青春期，睡眠节律常常在晚上向后推迟。

pos.zh: 名词：青春期；青少年时期；发育过渡阶段

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语现在分词 adolescens 加形容词后缀 -ent 构成，义为「青春期的」
由形容词 adolescent 转类为零派生名词，义为「青少年」
由 adolescent 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「以青春期的方式」，较少使用

senses.title: The period between childhood and adulthood
senses.titleCN: 青春期：童年与成年之间的时期
senses.definition: the period of life between childhood and adulthood, when a person grows toward maturity
senses.definitionCN: 童年与成年之间的生命阶段，人在此期间走向成熟
senses.example: Adolescence is often described as a bridge between childhood and adulthood.
senses.exampleCN: 青春期常被描述为连接童年与成年的桥梁。
senses.why: The core image is a sapling shooting up: the stem lengthens fast while the bark is still soft.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一棵迅速抽条的树苗：树干猛长，树皮还很软。

senses.title: The stage studied in psychology
senses.titleCN: 心理学意义上的青春期阶段
senses.definition: the developmental stage that psychology studies as a distinct period of mental growth
senses.definitionCN: 心理学作为一个独立的心智成长阶段来研究的时期
senses.example: Psychologists treat adolescence as a stage with its own tasks and conflicts.
senses.exampleCN: 心理学家把青春期看作一个有自身任务与冲突的阶段。
senses.why: The sapling is now observed rather than merely seen: the growth is divided into stages with names.
senses.whyCN: 树苗这时不只是被看见，而是被观察：生长被划分成有名称的阶段。

senses.title: The teenage years
senses.titleCN: 少年时期：十几岁的年月
senses.definition: the years of a person's teens, counted in ordinary speech rather than in theory
senses.definitionCN: 一个人十几岁的那几年，是日常说法而非理论划分
senses.example: She spent her adolescence in a small coastal town.
senses.exampleCN: 她的少年时期是在一个海边小镇度过的。
senses.why: Here the period is simply the stretch of years a person can point back to.
senses.whyCN: 这里的阶段就是一个人回头能指认出的那一段年月。

senses.title: A transitional period of growth
senses.definition: the transitional period in which a child's body and mind pass toward adult form
senses.definitionCN: 儿童的身体与心智向成年形态过渡的时期
senses.example: The clinic monitors growth throughout adolescence.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所会在整个发育过渡期监测生长情况。
senses.why: The sapling is between two states: no longer a seedling, not yet a full tree.
senses.whyCN: 树苗处在两种状态之间：不再是幼苗，也还不是成树。

senses.title: The bodily and emotional changes of that period
senses.definition: the physical and emotional changes that occur during this period
senses.definitionCN: 在这一时期发生的身体与情绪方面的变化
senses.example: Rapid mood shifts are common in early adolescence.
senses.exampleCN: 情绪快速起伏在青春期早期很常见。
senses.why: What is named here is not the time but what fills it: growth shows itself as change.
senses.whyCN: 这里命名的不是那段时间，而是填满它的东西：成长以变化的形式显现。

senses.title: Young people of that age as a group
senses.definition: young people of this age considered together as a social group
senses.definitionCN: 把这一年龄段的年轻人作为一个社会群体来看待
senses.example: The survey asked adolescents about health, school and family.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查询问了青春期人群关于健康、学校与家庭的情况。
senses.why: Many saplings standing together become a grove: the stage turns into a group.
senses.whyCN: 许多树苗站在一起就成了林子：阶段变成了人群。

senses.title: The social stage between child and adult roles
senses.definition: the social stage in which a person is no longer treated as a child but not yet as an adult
senses.definitionCN: 一个人不再被当作孩子、却还未被当作成年人的社会阶段
senses.example: In many societies adolescence is marked by new duties and fewer protections.
senses.exampleCN: 在许多社会里，青春期的标志是新的责任与更少的保护。
senses.why: The sapling has its own place in the orchard: the period is also a position in society.
senses.whyCN: 树苗在果园里有自己的位置：这个时期也是一种社会位置。

senses.title: The period ending in physical maturity
senses.titleCN: 生理成熟期：以身体成熟告终
senses.definition: the span of growth that ends when the body reaches full physical maturity
senses.definitionCN: 以身体达到完全生理成熟为终点的生长期
senses.example: Bone growth is usually complete by the end of adolescence.
senses.exampleCN: 骨骼生长通常在青春期结束时完成。
senses.why: The sapling finally hardens into timber: the period has a clear biological end.
senses.whyCN: 树苗最终硬化成材：这个时期有一个明确的生物学终点。

intro.en: Adolescence comes from Latin adolescentia, a noun of growing, and it still names growth rather than a fixed age.
intro.cn: adolescence 来自拉丁语 adolescentia，是一个表示「生长」的名词，至今指的生长过程而非固定年龄。

items.en: alescere was an inceptive verb meaning 'to begin to grow'; its stem is related to alere 'to nourish'.
items.cn: alescere 是一个表示「开始生长」的起始动词，其词干与 alere「滋养」有关。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus alescere gave adolescere, 'to grow up, come to maturity'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 alescere 构成 adolescere，意为「长大、成熟起来」。

items.en: The noun adolescentia meant 'youth, the time of growing up'; its exact first use is not recorded.
items.cn: 名词 adolescentia 意为「青年时期、成长的年月」；其确切的首见用例没有记录。

items.en: English borrowed the word through French, using it for the age of youth rather than for a single person.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入这个词，用来指青年的年岁，而不是指某一个人。

items.en: Medicine and psychology gave the period clearer boundaries, and the word now names a stage of development.
items.cn: 医学与心理学为这个时期划出更清晰的边界，这个词如今指一个发育阶段。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same growing root; the near-meaning group gathers other names for youth and its end point.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「生长」词根的一族词；近义组收其他表示青年及成熟终点的词。

entries.definition: A noun or adjective for a young person in this stage, or something typical of it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「青少年」或「青春期的」，指处在这一阶段的年轻人或其特征。

entries.definition: A grown person; Latin adultus is the past participle of the same verb 'to grow up'.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成年人」；拉丁语 adultus 正是同一个「长大」动词的过去分词。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in the manner of an adolescent; rare.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「以青少年的方式」，较少使用。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning reaching puberty; it looks close but comes from Latin pubes, not from alescere.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「进入青春期的」；看起来相近，却来自拉丁语 pubes，与 alescere 无关。

entries.definition: The biological process of becoming sexually mature; narrower and more physical than adolescence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「青春期、发身期」，指性成熟的过程，比 adolescence 更窄、更偏生理。

entries.definition: The time of being young, or young people collectively; broader and often warmer in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「青春、青年」，可指年轻时期或青年群体，范围更宽，语气常更温暖。

entries.definition: The years from thirteen to nineteen; a plain count of age rather than a stage of growth.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「十几岁」，只是对年龄的朴素计数，而不是成长阶段的划分。

entries.definition: The state reached at the end of growth; the far side of adolescence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成熟」，是生长结束时所达到的状态，正位于青春期之后。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb of growing up and the family it produced.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「长大」动词，以及它产生的词族。

normal.en: alescere means to begin to grow, so adolescence is the time when growing takes hold.
normal.cn: alescere 意为「开始生长」，所以 adolescence 就是生长真正发力的那段时期。

normal.en: Adolescent, adult and adolescence all descend from the same verb adolescere.
normal.cn: adolescent、adult、adolescence 都来自同一个动词 adolescere。

normal.en: Adolescence names the period, while adolescent names the person; the ending -ence marks a state.
normal.cn: adolescence 指那段时期，adolescent 指那个人；词尾 -ence 标记一种状态。

normal.en: Puberty is the physical core of adolescence, not a synonym for the whole stage.
normal.cn: puberty 是青春期的生理核心，并不等于整个阶段的同义词。

normal.en: Early adolescence and late adolescence split the same growth into two ends.
normal.cn: early adolescence 与 late adolescence 把同一段成长分成首尾两端。

abstract.en: Picture a young tree that has suddenly grown taller than the fence, yet still bends in a strong wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵小树突然长得比篱笆还高，却仍会被大风压弯。

abstract.en: The tree is neither seedling nor timber: that in-between state is the whole idea of adolescence.
abstract.cn: 这棵树既不是幼苗也不是木材：这种不上不下的状态，正是青春期这一概念的核心。

abstract.en: A whole grove of such trees is the age group; when the bark finally hardens, the period is over.
abstract.cn: 一整片这样的小树就是这一年龄群体；当树皮终于变硬，这段时期就结束了。

examples.en: During adolescence, friendships often matter more than almost anything else.
examples.cn: 在青春期，友谊常常比几乎任何东西都重要。

examples.en: She spent her adolescence in a small coastal town.
examples.cn: 她的少年时期是在一个海边小镇度过的。

examples.en: The study follows children through adolescence into adult life.
examples.cn: 这项研究追踪孩子们从青春期一直到成年生活。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿兜勒斯恩斯」——小树猛地蹿高，树皮还软，风一吹就晃

root: 拉丁语 adolescentia「青年时期」来自 adolescere「长大、成熟」，后者是 ad-「向」加 alescere「开始生长」，alescere 的词干又与 alere「滋养」相关。adult 的拉丁语 adultus 是同一个动词的过去分词。更早的印欧词根存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one stretch of growth: the period, its psychological stage, the teen years, the transition, its changes, its people, its social place, and its physical end.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述同一段成长：时期本身、心理学阶段、十几岁的年月、过渡、身心变化、人群、社会位置，以及生理终点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sapling shoots up fast while its bark is still soft and bends in the wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：树苗迅速拔高，树皮仍软，随风弯下。

branches.en: THE YEARS: the period itself and the plain stretch of teen years a person remembers.
branches.cn: 年月线：时期本身，以及一个人能回忆起的、朴素的十几岁岁月。

branches.en: THE STAGE: a named developmental step and the in-between transition of body and mind.
branches.cn: 阶段线：一个有名称的发育步骤，以及身心不上不下的过渡。

branches.en: THE BODY: the changes that fill the period, and the physical maturity that ends it.
branches.cn: 身体线：填满这段时期的变化，以及为它收尾的生理成熟。

branches.en: THE GROUP: many saplings standing together become a social category.
branches.cn: 群体线：许多树苗站在一起，就成为一个社会类别。

branches.en: THE POSITION: the stage is also a place in society, between child and adult roles.
branches.cn: 位置线：这个阶段也是社会中的一个位置，介于孩子与成人的角色之间。

intro.en: Adolescence is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin verb of growing, with a noun ending added in Latin.
intro.cn: adolescence 由拉丁语前缀、表示「生长」的拉丁动词，以及拉丁语名词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: alescere, adolescere, adolescens and adolescentia are recorded Latin forms; adulescens is a variant spelling of the participle.
latinIntro.cn: alescere、adolescere、adolescens、adolescentia 都是有记录的拉丁形式；adulescens 是分词的另一拼写。

items.example: It turns alescere into adolescere.
items.exampleCN: 它把 alescere 变成 adolescere。

items.example: The verb is the growing root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「生长」词根。

items.example: The compound verb is the direct source of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词是这一词族的直接来源。

items.example: The participle becomes the English adjective and noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成为英语的形容词与名词。

items.meaning: youth, the time of growing up
items.example: It is the Latin shape behind adolescence.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adolescence 背后的拉丁语形态。

items.example: It forms adolescence from the Latin noun stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由拉丁名词词干构成 adolescence。

items.example: It forms adolescent.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adolescent。

items.example: It forms adolescently.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adolescently。

latinEntries.meaning: youth, the time of growing up
