senses.title: A young person between childhood and adulthood
senses.definition: a young person who is no longer a child but not yet an adult
senses.definitionCN: 已不再是孩子、但还不是成年人的年轻人
senses.example: The adolescent beside her kept checking his phone.
senses.exampleCN: 她身旁那个青少年不停地看着手机。
senses.why: The core image is a figure with a schoolbag under a street lamp: tall already, but still narrow at the shoulders.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是路灯下背着书包的身影：个子已经高了，肩膀却还窄。

senses.title: Relating to the teenage years
senses.definition: relating to the period between childhood and adulthood, used to describe things of that stage
senses.definitionCN: 与童年到成年之间的时期有关，用于描述该阶段的特征
senses.example: Adolescent behaviour can change quickly from week to week.
senses.exampleCN: 青春期的行为可能一周一周地变化。
senses.why: The same figure now becomes a lens: the word describes whatever belongs to that stage.
senses.whyCN: 同一个人这时变成了一面透镜：这个词用来描述属于那个阶段的一切。

senses.title: Still growing physically
senses.definition: still in the process of physical growth, not yet fully formed
senses.definitionCN: 仍处在身体生长过程中，尚未完全成形
senses.example: Adolescent bones are more easily injured during heavy training.
senses.exampleCN: 发育中的骨骼在强度训练中更容易受伤。
senses.why: The schoolbag figure is still lengthening: the body has not finished its work.
senses.whyCN: 背书包的身影还在拔高：身体尚未完成它的工程。

senses.title: Not yet mature in behaviour
senses.definition: used critically of behaviour that seems childish or emotionally immature
senses.definitionCN: 带批评意味，指行为显得孩子气、情绪上不成熟
senses.example: His adolescent sulking made the meeting harder.
senses.exampleCN: 他那不成熟的赌气让会议更难进行。
senses.why: The growing stage is extended into a judgement: what should have been outgrown is still there.
senses.whyCN: 成长的阶段被延伸成一种评判：本该已经长过去的东西还留在身上。

senses.title: Adolescents as a group
senses.definition: young people of this age considered together as a group or population
senses.definitionCN: 把这一年龄段的年轻人作为一个群体或人口来看待
senses.example: The campaign was designed for adolescents rather than for their parents.
senses.exampleCN: 这场宣传活动是为青少年群体而不是为他们的父母设计的。
senses.why: One figure becomes a crowd at the school gate: the stage turns into a group.
senses.whyCN: 一个身影在校门口变成一群：阶段变成了群体。

senses.title: Behaviour typical of that age
senses.definition: the kind of behaviour that is usual or expected at this age
senses.definitionCN: 在这个年龄常见或可预期的行为方式
senses.example: Risk-taking is often seen as an adolescent pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 冒险常被视为一种青春期行为模式。
senses.why: The group's habits become a pattern: what many do at that age is named after the age.
senses.whyCN: 群体的习惯成了模式：许多人在那个年龄做的事，就以那个年龄来命名。

senses.title: A subject of adolescent psychology
senses.titleCN: 青少年心理学的研究对象
senses.definition: in psychology, a young person of this stage considered as a subject of study and care
senses.definitionCN: 心理学上，把这一阶段的年轻人作为研究与关怀的对象
senses.example: The clinic treats each adolescent as a person with rights, not only a case.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所把每个青少年当作有权利的人，而不只是一个病例。
senses.why: The figure is now placed under a professional gaze: the word names who is being studied.
senses.whyCN: 这个身影此时被置于专业的目光之下：这个词指明被研究的对象是谁。

senses.title: The physical features of that stage
senses.definition: the physical characteristics that belong to this stage of development
senses.definitionCN: 属于这一发育阶段的生理特征
senses.example: Adolescent growth spurts vary widely in timing.
senses.exampleCN: 青春期的生长突增在时间上差异很大。
senses.why: The word turns to the body itself: the lengthening limbs are the most visible sign of the stage.
senses.whyCN: 这个词转向身体本身：抽长的四肢是这个阶段最显眼的标志。

intro.en: Adolescent is the Latin present participle 'growing up' borrowed into English as both a noun and an adjective.
intro.cn: adolescent 是拉丁语现在分词「正在长大」被借入英语，同时用作名词与形容词。

items.en: alescere meant 'to begin to grow'; its stem is related to alere 'to nourish'.
items.cn: alescere 意为「开始生长」，其词干与 alere「滋养」有关。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus alescere gave adolescere, 'to grow up, come to maturity'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 alescere 构成 adolescere，意为「长大、成熟起来」。

items.en: The present participle adolescens meant 'growing up' and was also used as a noun for a young person; adulescens is an older spelling.
items.cn: 现在分词 adolescens 意为「正在长大的」，也作名词指年轻人；adulescens 是较早的拼写。

items.en: English borrowed the word through French and used it both for the person and for what belongs to the age.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入这个词，既用来指人，也用来指属于这个年龄的事物。

items.en: The noun settled as a neutral term for a young person, while the adjective also grew a critical, immature sense.
items.cn: 名词固定为指年轻人的中性说法，而形容词又发展出带批评意味的「不成熟」义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the growing root; the near-meaning group gathers other names for a young person or for immaturity.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「生长」词根的一族词；近义组收其他指年轻人或不成熟的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the period itself, not for the person living through it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「青春期」，指时期本身，而不是经历这个时期的人。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in the manner of an adolescent; rare.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「以青少年的方式」，较少使用。

entries.definition: A grown person; Latin adultus is the past participle of the same verb adolescere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成年人」；拉丁语 adultus 是同一个动词 adolescere 的过去分词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning reaching puberty; it looks close but comes from Latin pubes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「进入青春期的」；看起来相近，却来自拉丁语 pubes，词源不同。

entries.definition: A person aged thirteen to nineteen; an age count rather than a developmental stage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「十几岁的青少年」，是按年龄计数，而非按发育阶段划分。

entries.definition: A young person or young people in general; often warmer and less clinical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「青年、年轻人」，常更温和，少些学术色彩。

entries.definition: A young person, especially in legal contexts; also used of childish behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「少年」，多用于法律语境，也可形容幼稚的行为。

entries.definition: Not fully developed, physically or emotionally; the critical sense of adolescent.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不成熟的」，指身体或情绪尚未充分发展，正对应 adolescent 的引申义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin participle and the difference between the person and the period.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语分词，以及「人」与「时期」之间的区别。

normal.en: Adolescens is a present participle, so an adolescent is literally 'one growing up'.
normal.cn: adolescens 是现在分词，所以 an adolescent 字面上就是「一个正在长大的人」。

normal.en: Adolescence is the period; adolescent is the person or the adjective.
normal.cn: adolescence 是时期；adolescent 是人或形容词。

normal.en: Adult comes from the past participle of the same verb, so adult and adolescent are two ends of one growth.
normal.cn: adult 来自同一个动词的过去分词，所以 adult 与 adolescent 是同一次生长的两端。

normal.en: Adolescent boys and adolescent behaviour keep the adjective attached to the stage.
normal.cn: adolescent boys 与 adolescent behaviour 都把形容词固定在这个阶段上。

normal.en: The critical sense is plain in a phrase like adolescent sulking.
normal.cn: 批评性的「不成熟」义，在 adolescent sulking 这样的说法里一目了然。

abstract.en: Picture a schoolbag silhouette under a street lamp: tall enough to reach the sign, narrow enough to be blown sideways by wind.
abstract.cn: 想象路灯下背着书包的剪影：高得够到标牌，肩窄得会被风侧吹。

abstract.en: When one such figure becomes many at the school gate, the person turns into a group.
abstract.cn: 当这样一个身影在校门口变成许多个，人就成了群体。

abstract.en: When the shoulders finally broaden, the word no longer fits, and adult takes its place.
abstract.cn: 当肩膀终于变宽，这个词就不再合适，adult 接替了它的位置。

examples.en: The adolescent sat alone at the back of the bus.
examples.cn: 那个青少年独自坐在公交车后排。

examples.en: Teachers need patience with adolescent moods.
examples.cn: 教师需要耐心对待青少年的情绪起伏。

examples.en: Adolescent growth varies greatly from one child to another.
examples.cn: 青春期的生长在不同孩子身上差异很大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿兜勒斯恩特」——路灯下背书包的少年，个子高了，肩膀还窄

root: 拉丁语 adolescens 是 adolescere「长大」的现在分词，字面意为「正在长大的」，也可作名词指年轻人；adolescere 由 ad-「向」加 alescere「开始生长」构成。adult 的拉丁语 adultus 是同一动词的过去分词，因此两词是同一生长过程的两端。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all focus on one growing figure: the person, the stage, the growing body, immaturity, the group, its behaviour, the studied subject, and the physical signs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都聚焦同一个正在长大的身影：这个人、这个阶段、发育中的身体、不成熟、群体、行为模式、研究中的对象，以及生理标志。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a schoolbag figure under a street lamp, tall already but still narrow at the shoulders.
core.cn: 核心意象：路灯下背着书包的身影，个子已高，肩膀仍窄。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a single young figure standing between two stages of life.
branches.cn: 人物线：一个站在人生两个阶段之间的年轻身影。

branches.en: THE STAGE: whatever belongs to the age, including its visible bodily signs.
branches.cn: 阶段线：属于这个年龄的一切，包括明显的身体标志。

branches.en: THE GROWTH AND ITS SHADOW: a body still forming, and behaviour that has not caught up.
branches.cn: 生长与其阴影：仍在成形的身体，以及还没跟上的行为。

branches.en: THE CROWD: one figure becomes a group with recognisable habits.
branches.cn: 人群线：一个身影变成一群，并带上可辨识的习惯。

branches.en: THE GAZE: psychology and medicine study this person as a subject with rights.
branches.cn: 目光线：心理学与医学把这个人当作有权利的研究对象。

intro.en: Adolescent is a Latin participle that became an English noun and adjective; its family shares the same growing root.
intro.cn: adolescent 是一个成为英语名词与形容词的拉丁语分词，其词族共享同一个「生长」词根。

latinIntro.en: alescere, adolescere, adolescens and adultus are all recorded Latin forms, so nothing here is invented.
latinIntro.cn: alescere、adolescere、adolescens、adultus 都是有记录的拉丁形式，此处没有臆造成分。

items.example: It turns alescere into adolescere.
items.exampleCN: 它把 alescere 变成 adolescere。

items.example: The verb is the growing root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「生长」词根。

items.example: The compound verb is the source of both adolescent and adult.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词是 adolescent 与 adult 的共同来源。

items.example: The participle is the direct source of adolescent.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词是 adolescent 的直接来源。

items.example: It marks the participle form in English.
items.exampleCN: 它在英语中保留了分词的形式。

items.example: It forms adolescence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adolescence。

items.example: It forms adolescently.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adolescently。

items.structure: English adjective and noun from Latin
items.example: Adult is the other end of the same growth.
items.exampleCN: adult 是同一次生长的另一端。

definition_zh: 收养（孩子）；采取（方法或态度）；正式通过（法案）；采纳建议；采用技术；承继习俗；选为候选人；采用新名称
definition_en: to take a child, method, decision, or name as one's own and begin to use or raise it
core_image: 一双陌生的手伸过来，把一个孩子牵回家：从此他被当作自家的
scene: 社区活动室里，一对夫妻认真听着工作人员讲解领养手续，桌上摊着一叠表格。They decided to adopt a child from the local orphanage.
sceneCN: 这里 adopt 是「收养孩子」（第 1 个义项：依法把别人的孩子当作自己的孩子抚养）；句意为他们决定从当地孤儿院收养一个孩子。

pos.zh: 动词：收养；采取；通过；采纳；采用

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「收养；采用；通过」
由 adopt 加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「收养的；领养的」
由 adopt 加表示受动者的后缀 -ee 构成，义为「被收养者」
由 adopt 加表示施动者的后缀 -er 构成，义为「收养人；采用者」
由 adopt 加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「可收养的；可采用的」

senses.title: To take another person's child as one's own
senses.definition: to take another person's child into one's family and raise it as one's own
senses.definitionCN: 把别人的孩子接入自己的家庭，当作自己的孩子抚养
senses.example: They decided to adopt a child from the local orphanage.
senses.exampleCN: 他们决定从当地孤儿院收养一个孩子。
senses.why: The core image is a hand reaching across: someone outside the family is drawn inside and given a place.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一只手伸过去：原本在家庭之外的人被牵进来，得到一个位置。

senses.title: To take up a method or attitude
senses.definition: to begin to use a particular method, attitude, or way of behaving
senses.definitionCN: 开始采用某种方法、态度或行为方式
senses.example: The team adopted a slower, more careful approach.
senses.exampleCN: 团队采取了一种更慢、更谨慎的做法。
senses.why: The reaching hand now grasps not a person but a practice, and keeps it as its own.
senses.whyCN: 伸出的手这时抓的不是人，而是一种做法，并把它当作自己的保留下来。

senses.title: To pass a law or rule formally
senses.definition: to approve and formally accept a law, rule, or official plan
senses.definitionCN: 批准并正式接受一项法律、规则或官方计划
senses.example: The council adopted the new housing policy last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会去年春天通过了新的住房政策。
senses.why: A document is taken up by a body of people: what was proposed outside now belongs to the institution.
senses.whyCN: 一份文件被一个机构接了过来：原本在外面被提议的东西，如今属于这个机构。

senses.title: To accept a suggestion
senses.definition: to accept someone's suggestion and act on it
senses.definitionCN: 接受某人的建议并付诸实行
senses.example: The editor adopted most of her suggestions.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑采纳了她的大部分建议。
senses.why: The hand reaches toward another person's idea: the idea is brought in and made the speaker's own.
senses.whyCN: 手伸向另一个人的想法：想法被带进来，成为说话者自己的。

senses.title: To start using a technology
senses.definition: to begin to use a new technology, tool, or system in practice
senses.definitionCN: 在实践中开始使用一种新技术、工具或系统
senses.example: Many schools have adopted online teaching tools.
senses.exampleCN: 许多学校已经采用在线教学工具。
senses.why: A tool is taken into the working hand and kept there until it becomes ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 工具被接进干活的那只手里，一直保留到它变得寻常。

senses.title: To take on a custom or habit
senses.definition: to take on a custom, habit, or style that came from elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 承接来自别处的习俗、习惯或风格
senses.example: The village adopted the custom of lighting lanterns at midsummer.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子承继了仲夏点灯的传统。
senses.why: A practice is inherited by a hand that never made it: the custom is taken over and kept alive.
senses.whyCN: 一种做法被一只并非创造它的手接了过去：习俗被接管，并继续活着。

senses.title: To select a candidate
senses.definition: to choose someone as a candidate for an election or post
senses.definitionCN: 选定某人为选举或职位的候选人
senses.example: The local party adopted him as its candidate for the seat.
senses.exampleCN: 当地政党选定他为该席位的候选人。
senses.why: A person is taken up by a party and presented as its own: choosing here means claiming.
senses.whyCN: 一个人被政党接了过去，并作为自己的人推出：这里的「选择」意味着「宣称归属」。

senses.title: To take a new name
senses.definition: to begin to use a new name, title, or spelling for oneself or something else
senses.definitionCN: 开始为自己或别的事物使用新的名称、头衔或拼写
senses.example: The company adopted a shorter name for its overseas market.
senses.exampleCN: 公司为海外市场采用了一个更短的名称。
senses.why: Even a name can be picked up and worn: what is adopted becomes the label one answers to.
senses.whyCN: 连名字也能被拿起、穿在身上：被采用的东西，成了自己应答的那个标签。

intro.en: Adopt is Latin adoptare, built from ad- and a verb meaning 'to choose'; choosing and taking as one's own are the same act here.
intro.cn: adopt 来自拉丁语 adoptare，由 ad- 与表示「选择」的动词构成；在这里，「选择」与「据为己有」是同一个动作。

items.en: optare meant 'to choose, wish, desire'; its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: optare 意为「选择、希望、想要」；其更早的来源不确定。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus optare gave adoptare, 'to choose for oneself, take as one's own'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 optare 构成 adoptare，意为「为自己挑选、据为己有」。

items.en: The noun adoptio named the legal act of taking a child into a family.
items.cn: 名词 adoptio 指把孩子接入家庭这一法律行为。

items.en: English borrowed the verb through French; the legal sense of taking a child came first, and other senses followed.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入这个动词；先有「收养孩子」的法律义，其他义项随后出现。

items.en: The word widened from children to methods, laws, technologies, customs, candidates and names.
items.cn: 这个词从孩子扩展到方法、法律、技术、习俗、候选人和名称。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adoption family and its Latin cousin opt; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of taking up and accepting.
note.cn: 形近组收 adoption 词族及其拉丁同族词 opt；近义组收表示「拿起、接受」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of adopting a child or taking up a practice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收养、采用、通过」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning related by adoption rather than by birth.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「收养的、领养的」，指因收养而非血缘形成的关系。

entries.definition: A person who adopts a child or takes up a new practice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收养人、采用者」。

entries.definition: A person who has been adopted.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「被收养者」。

entries.definition: To choose one thing rather than another; it shares the Latin verb optare.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「选择」，与本词共享拉丁动词 optare。

entries.definition: To accept an idea or change willingly; warmer and more enthusiastic than adopt.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欣然接受」，指乐意接纳某种观念或变化，比 adopt 更热情。

entries.definition: To begin doing or using something; plainer and less formal than adopt.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，义为「开始从事、开始使用」，比 adopt 朴素、少些正式色彩。

entries.definition: To give official agreement to a plan or law; close to the law sense of adopt.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「批准」，与 adopt 的法律义接近。

entries.definition: To care for a child without becoming a legal parent; not the same as adopt.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「寄养、临时抚养」，并不取得法律上的父母身份，与 adopt 不同。

entries.definition: To take on a role, name, or attitude; often without the idea of choice.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承担、采用（角色、名称、态度）」，常不含「挑选」的意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb 'to choose' that sits inside adopt.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用藏在 adopt 里的、真实的拉丁语动词「选择」。

normal.en: optare means to choose, so adopt is to choose something and make it your own.
normal.cn: optare 意为「选择」，所以 adopt 就是选中某物并把它变成自己的。

normal.en: Adoption, adoptive, adopter and adoptee all keep the adopt- base.
normal.cn: adoption、adoptive、adopter、adoptee 都保留 adopt- 词基。

normal.en: A council adopts a policy, while a family adopts a child; the same hand reaches out.
normal.cn: 议会 adopt 一项政策，家庭 adopt 一个孩子；伸出的都是同一只手。

normal.en: Foster is not adopt: a foster parent cares for a child without a legal claim.
normal.cn: foster 不等于 adopt：寄养父母照料孩子，却没有法律上的归属。

normal.en: To adopt a name is to pick it up and answer to it from then on.
normal.cn: adopt a name 就是拿起一个名字，从此用它应答。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching across a threshold and drawing something inside: a child, a method, a law, a name.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸过门槛，把东西牵进里面：孩子、方法、法律、名字皆可。

abstract.en: What is adopted is not merely borrowed; it is kept and treated as one's own.
abstract.cn: 被 adopt 的东西不只是借来，而是被保留下来，并被当作自己的。

abstract.en: The old Latin verb inside is 'to choose': adoption is a choice that changes who belongs to whom.
abstract.cn: 里面那个古老拉丁动词意为「选择」：收养是一种改变归属关系的选择。

examples.en: The couple adopted a girl from a nearby village.
examples.cn: 这对夫妻从附近村子收养了一个女孩。

examples.en: The council adopted the new housing policy last spring.
examples.cn: 市议会去年春天通过了新的住房政策。

examples.en: Many schools have adopted online teaching tools.
examples.cn: 许多学校已经采用在线教学工具。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额的奥普特」——一只手伸过去，把孩子、方法或名字牵进自家门

root: 拉丁语 adoptare「挑选过来、据为己有」由 ad-「向」加 optare「选择」构成；其名词 adoptio 本指把孩子接入家庭的法律行为。英语经法语借入后，词义由「收养」扩展到「采取方法、通过法案、采纳建议、采用名称」。optare 更早的词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all perform one reach: a child, a method, a law, a suggestion, a technology, a custom, a candidate, and a name are taken and kept as one's own.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在做同一个伸手动作：孩子、方法、法律、建议、技术、习俗、候选人、名称，被拿起并当作自己的保留下来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaches across a threshold and draws something inside, where it will be treated as one's own.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸过门槛，把某物牵进里面，从此被当作自己的。

branches.en: THE CHILD: a person from outside a family is brought in and raised as its own.
branches.cn: 孩子线：原本在家庭之外的人被牵进来，当作自家人抚养。

branches.en: THE PRACTICE: a method or a technology is picked up and used until it is ordinary.
branches.cn: 做法线：一种方法或技术被拿起使用，直到它变得寻常。

branches.en: THE LAW: a proposed rule is taken up by a body and becomes binding.
branches.cn: 法律线：一项被提议的规则由某个机构接手，从而具有约束力。

branches.en: THE INHERITANCE: a suggestion or a custom is taken over from someone else.
branches.cn: 承接线：一项建议或一种习俗，从别人那里接过来。

branches.en: THE CLAIM: a candidate or a name is presented as belonging to the one who chose it.
branches.cn: 归属线：候选人或名称被推出，宣称属于做出选择的那一方。

intro.en: Adopt is a Latin compound verb; English then builds a whole family of nouns, adjectives and agent words on it.
intro.cn: adopt 是一个拉丁复合动词，英语随后在它之上建起名词、形容词与施动者的一整族词。

latinIntro.en: optare, adoptare and adoptio are recorded Latin words; the list below is historical, not reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: optare、adoptare、adoptio 都是有记录的拉丁词，下面所列属于历史形式，而非重构。

items.example: It turns optare into adoptare.
items.exampleCN: 它把 optare 变成 adoptare。

items.example: The verb is the choosing root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「选择」词根。

items.example: It is the direct source of adopt.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adopt 的直接来源。

items.example: It is the Latin shape behind adoption.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adoption 背后的拉丁语形态。

items.example: It forms adoption.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adoption。

items.example: It forms adoptive.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adoptive。

items.example: It forms adoptee.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adoptee。

items.example: It forms adopter.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adopter。

items.example: It forms adoptable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adoptable。

definition_zh: 热爱；崇拜；爱慕；喜爱（口语）；敬奉神；喜爱做；极喜欢；仰慕赞美
definition_en: to love and admire someone or something very much, or to worship a god with devotion
core_image: 烛光前低头合掌：把心里最高的位置留给所敬所爱之物
scene: 海边的老教堂里，烛光排成一行，信徒们低头合掌，空气里只有蜡香。The pilgrims adored the wooden statue in silence.
sceneCN: 这里 adore 是「敬奉圣物」（第 5 个义项：以宗教礼节对圣像表达敬意）；句意为朝圣者默默地敬奉那尊木像。

pos.zh: 动词：热爱；崇拜；爱慕；喜爱；敬奉

collocations.phrase: adore the ground somebody walks on
collocations.zh: 对某人崇拜得五体投地

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词基 ador- 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「崇敬；热爱；爱慕」
由 adore 加表示施动者的后缀 -er 构成，义为「崇拜者；爱慕者」
由 adore 加现在分词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「充满爱意的；崇敬的」
由 adoring 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「充满爱意地」
由 adore 加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「可爱的；讨人喜欢的」

senses.title: To love someone very much
senses.definition: to love someone very much, with warmth and delight rather than solemnity
senses.definitionCN: 非常爱某人，带着温暖与喜悦，而不是庄严肃穆
senses.example: She adores her grandchildren and spoils them shamelessly.
senses.exampleCN: 她非常疼爱孙辈，毫无顾忌地宠着他们。
senses.why: The core image is hands folded before a candle: the highest place in the heart is given away.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是在烛光前合掌：心里最高的位置被让了出去。

senses.title: To worship a god
senses.definition: to honour a god with religious worship and devotion
senses.definitionCN: 以宗教敬拜与虔诚敬奉神明
senses.example: The villagers still adore the old goddess of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们仍然崇拜那条河的老女神。
senses.why: The folded hands are now raised to a deity: love is directed upward and outward.
senses.whyCN: 合掌的手这时朝向神祇：爱被指向上方与外在。

senses.title: To feel romantic devotion
senses.definition: to feel deep romantic love and devotion toward someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人怀有深切的爱恋与倾慕
senses.example: He adored her from the first evening they met.
senses.exampleCN: 从相识的第一个晚上起，他就爱慕着她。
senses.why: The highest place is given to one person, and the feeling is both tender and a little worshipful.
senses.whyCN: 最高的位置被让给某一个人，这份情感既温柔，又带一点膜拜意味。

senses.title: To like something very much in speech
senses.definition: in everyday speech, to like a thing or place very much in a warm, informal way
senses.definitionCN: 在日常口语中，以温暖随意的方式非常喜欢某物或某地
senses.example: I adore that little café on the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 我特别喜欢街角那家小咖啡馆。
senses.why: The solemn gesture relaxes into a smile: the same word now carries everyday pleasure.
senses.whyCN: 庄重的姿势放松成一个微笑：同一个词如今承载日常的愉悦。

senses.title: To reverence a sacred image
senses.definition: to show religious reverence to a sacred image, relic, or shrine with ritual acts
senses.definitionCN: 以仪式性的举动对圣像、圣物或圣所表达宗教敬意
senses.example: The pilgrims adored the wooden statue in silence.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者默默地敬奉那尊木像。
senses.why: The hands are folded before an object rather than a person: devotion becomes a ritual.
senses.whyCN: 合掌的对象是一件物品而非一个人：虔诚变成了仪式。

senses.title: To enjoy doing something
senses.definition: in the pattern adore doing something, to enjoy an activity very much
senses.definitionCN: 用于 adore doing something 结构，表示非常喜欢某项活动
senses.example: She adores walking along the shore at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 她非常喜欢黎明时沿着海岸散步。
senses.why: The thing loved is now an action: the heart gives its highest place to a way of spending time.
senses.whyCN: 所爱之物此时是一个动作：心把最高的位置让给一种度过时间的方式。

senses.title: To be extremely fond of something
senses.titleCN: 极喜欢（某种食物或嗜好）
senses.definition: to have a strong, settled fondness for a particular food, object, or pastime
senses.definitionCN: 对某种食物、物品或消遣怀有强烈而固定的喜爱
senses.example: He adores chocolate and keeps a bar in his desk drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 他极喜欢巧克力，抽屉里总放着一块。
senses.why: A small, repeated pleasure takes the place of the god: the word's warmth settles on a habit.
senses.whyCN: 一种细小而反复的愉悦取代了神的位置：这个词的温热落在一种习惯上。

senses.title: To admire and praise intensely
senses.definition: to admire someone intensely and speak of them with great praise
senses.definitionCN: 极其仰慕某人，并以高度的赞美谈论其人
senses.example: The crowd adored the young singer and would not let her leave.
senses.exampleCN: 人群极度仰慕这位年轻歌手，不让她离开。
senses.why: The upward gaze and the folded hands combine: admiration becomes something close to worship.
senses.whyCN: 仰望的目光与合掌的姿态叠在一起：钦佩变得近乎崇拜。

intro.en: Adore comes from Latin adorare, a verb of speaking to a god, and its oldest sense is prayer rather than affection.
intro.cn: adore 来自拉丁语 adorare，本是一个对神说话的动词，最古老的意思是祈祷，而不是爱意。

items.en: orare meant 'to speak, plead, pray'; it is also the source of orator and oration.
items.cn: orare 意为「说话、恳求、祈祷」，也是 orator 与 oration 的来源。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus orare gave adorare, 'to speak to, pray to, worship'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 orare 构成 adorare，意为「对……说话、向……祈祷、敬拜」。

items.en: The noun adoratio named worship and the act of praying to a deity.
items.cn: 名词 adoratio 表示敬拜以及对神祈祷的行为。

items.en: Old French adorer kept the religious sense, and English took the word from it in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 古法语 adorer 保留了宗教义，英语在中世纪从它借入这个词。

items.en: The meaning widened from worship to deep love, and then to everyday fondness for things and activities.
items.cn: 词义从「敬拜」扩展到深切的爱，再扩展到对事物与活动的日常喜爱。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same orare root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of love, worship, and esteem.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 orare 词根的一族词；近义组收表示爱、崇拜与敬重的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for deep love, worship, or reverence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「崇敬、热爱、爱慕」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning lovable or charming; much lighter than adore.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可爱的、讨人喜欢的」，语气比 adore 轻得多。

entries.definition: An adjective describing a look or person full of love and reverence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「充满爱意的、崇敬的」，用于描述目光或人。

entries.definition: A person who adores someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「崇拜者、爱慕者」。

entries.definition: A skilled public speaker; it comes from the same Latin verb 'to speak'.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「演说家」，同出拉丁语中表示「说话」的动词。

entries.definition: To honour a god or person with devotion; the religious core of adore.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「崇拜、敬奉」，正对应 adore 的宗教核心义。

entries.definition: To feel deep affection for someone; broader and plainer than adore.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「爱」，比 adore 更宽、更朴素。

entries.definition: To treasure and care for someone or something; gentler and less exalted.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「珍爱、珍惜」，更温柔，也没有那么高的崇敬意味。

entries.definition: To feel deep respect and awe; solemn and mainly about esteem.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「崇敬」，庄重，主要强调敬意。

entries.definition: To admire someone excessively as an idol; stronger and often critical.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「把……当偶像崇拜」，程度更强，常带批评意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb 'to pray' and the family that grew from it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语动词「祈祷」，以及由它长出的词族。

normal.en: orare means to speak and pray, so adore began as speaking to a god.
normal.cn: orare 意为「说话、祈祷」，所以 adore 最初是「对神说话」。

normal.en: Oration, orator and adore share the same speaking root.
normal.cn: oration、orator 与 adore 共享同一个「说话」词根。

normal.en: Adoration and adorer keep the ador- base; adorable adds -able and becomes much lighter.
normal.cn: adoration 与 adorer 保留 ador- 词基；adorable 加了 -able，语气轻得多。

normal.en: Adore doing something is the pattern for activities, as in adore walking at dawn.
normal.cn: adore doing something 是表达喜爱活动的结构，如 adore walking at dawn。

normal.en: I adore chocolate is everyday fondness, not religious worship.
normal.cn: I adore chocolate 是日常的喜爱，并非宗教崇拜。

abstract.en: Picture a candle, two folded hands, and a head lowered: the body gives the highest place away.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛、合起的双手、低下的头：身体把最高的位置让了出去。

abstract.en: The same gesture can be turned toward a god, a lover, a singer, or a bar of chocolate.
abstract.cn: 同一个姿态可以朝向神、爱人、歌手，或一块巧克力。

abstract.en: The lower the head, the higher the object: that is why adore slides so easily from worship into fondness.
abstract.cn: 头低得越低，对象就越高：这正是 adore 能从敬拜轻易滑向喜爱的原因。

examples.en: She adores her grandchildren and spoils them shamelessly.
examples.cn: 她非常疼爱孙辈，毫无顾忌地宠着他们。

examples.en: I adore walking along the shore at dawn.
examples.cn: 我非常喜欢黎明时沿着海岸散步。

examples.en: The villagers still adore the old goddess of the river.
examples.cn: 村民们仍然崇拜那条河的老女神。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额的朵」——烛光前低头合掌，把心里最高的位置让给所敬所爱

root: 拉丁语 adorare「向……祈祷、敬拜」由 ad-「向」加 orare「说话、恳求、祈祷」构成；orare 也是 orator「演说家」与 oration「演说」的来源。英语经古法语 adorer 借入，词义由「敬拜」扩展到深切的爱，再扩展到日常喜爱。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all lower the head before something: a person loved, a god worshipped, a lover adored, a café liked, a relic revered, an activity enjoyed, a food craved, and a star admired.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在某物面前低下头：所爱的人、所崇拜的神、所爱慕的人、所喜欢的咖啡馆、所敬奉的圣物、所喜爱的活动、所贪恋的食物、所仰慕的明星。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands are folded before a candle, and the highest place in the heart is given away.
core.cn: 核心意象：在烛光前合掌，心里最高的位置被让了出去。

branches.en: THE BELOVED: a grandchild or a lover receives the highest place, warm and a little worshipful.
branches.cn: 所爱者线：孙辈或爱人得到最高的位置，既温暖又带一点膜拜。

branches.en: THE SACRED: a god or a relic is honoured with prayer and ritual.
branches.cn: 神圣线：神明或圣物以祈祷与仪式受到敬奉。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY: a café or a bar of chocolate takes the same warm place in smaller form.
branches.cn: 日常线：咖啡馆或一块巧克力，以更小的形式占据同样温热的位置。

branches.en: THE ACTIVITY: an action one loves to do is given the place of honour.
branches.cn: 活动线：一件爱做的事被让到尊位。

branches.en: THE STAR: admiration for a person grows until it almost becomes worship.
branches.cn: 明星线：对某人的钦佩不断增长，几乎变成崇拜。

intro.en: Adore is built from a Latin prefix and a verb of prayer; English adds the familiar noun, adjective and adverb endings.
intro.cn: adore 由拉丁语前缀与表示「祈祷」的动词构成，英语再添加常见的名词、形容词与副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: orare, adorare and adoratio are recorded Latin words; orator shares the same speaking root.
latinIntro.cn: orare、adorare、adoratio 都是有记录的拉丁词，orator 共享同一个「说话」词根。

items.exampleCN: 它把 orare 变成 adorare。

items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「说话」词根。

items.exampleCN: 它是 adore 的直接来源。

items.exampleCN: 它是 adoration 背后的拉丁语形态。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 adoringly。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 adorable。
